chunks: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who dies — what would he be entitled to from his wealth. So he said: 'For him is one-third of his wealth, and for the woman as well.'

key_terms.الرَّجُلُ يَمُوتُ: The man who dies — used as a jurisprudential query about a dying person's rights over their estate
key_terms.الْمَرْأَة: The woman — affirming equal right of women to bequeath one-third of their estate
key_terms.ثُلُثُ مَالِهِ: One-third of his wealth — the maximum permitted testamentary bequest in Islamic law

ai.seo_question: How much of their wealth can a Muslim bequeath in a will according to Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Shu'ayb ibn Ya'qub asked Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about the portion of a person's wealth they may bequeath by will before death. The Imam clarified that both a man and a woman are entitled to dispose of one-third of their estate. This hadith establishes the Shia jurisprudential principle that the testamentary bequest (wasiyyah) is limited to one-third of the estate, consistent with Quranic inheritance law, and explicitly affirms that women hold the same right as men in this regard.
